sanskrit: sa bhinnahṛdayo rājā bhagadattaḥ kirīṭinā śarāsanaṃ śarāṃś caiva gatāsuḥ pramumoca ha
english: King Bhagadatta, his heart pierced through by the Diademed One, let fall his bow and his arrows even as the life went out of him.

sanskrit: śirasas tasya vibhraṣṭaḥ papāta ca varāṅkuśaḥ nālatāḍanavibhraṣṭaṃ palāśaṃ nalinād iva
english: From his head the fine elephant-goad slipped loose and fell, as a petal falls from a lotus when the stalk is struck.

sanskrit: sa hemamālī tapanīyabhāṇḍāt; papāta nāgād girisaṃnikāśāt supuṣpito mārutavegarugṇo; mahīdharāgrād iva karṇikāraḥ
english: Garlanded in gold, he fell from the mountain-like elephant with its gilded trappings, like a karṇikāra tree in full blossom snapped by the rushing wind from the summit of a hill.

sanskrit: nihatya taṃ narapatim indravikramaṃ; sakhāyam indrasya tathaindrir āhave tato 'parāṃs tava jayakāṅkṣiṇo narān; babhañja vāyur balavān drumān iva
english: Having slain in battle that lord of men, valorous as Indra and Indra's own friend, the son of Indra then broke the rest of your warriors who longed for victory, as a mighty wind shatters the trees.

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca priyam indrasya satataṃ sakhāyam amitaujasam hatvā prāgjyotiṣaṃ pārthaḥ pradakṣiṇam avartata
english: Saṃjaya said: Having slain the lord of Prāgjyotiṣa, the ever-dear friend of Indra and a man of measureless might, Pārtha circled him reverently to the right.

sanskrit: tato gāndhārarājasya sutau parapuraṃjayau ārchetām arjunaṃ saṃkhye bhrātarau vṛṣakācalau
english: Then the two sons of the king of Gāndhāra, conquerors of hostile cities, the brothers Vṛṣaka and Acala, came upon Arjuna in the fray.

sanskrit: tau sametyārjunaṃ vīrau puraḥ paścāc ca dhanvinau avidhyetāṃ mahāvegair niśitair āśugair bhṛśam
english: The two heroic bowmen, closing upon Arjuna from before and from behind, pierced him sorely with swift, sharp, fast-flying shafts.

sanskrit: vṛṣakasya hayān sūtaṃ dhanuś chatraṃ rathaṃ dhvajam tilaśo vyadhamat pārthaḥ saubalasya śitaiḥ śaraiḥ
english: With his keen arrows Pārtha shredded to bits the horses, the charioteer, the bow, the parasol, the car, and the banner of Vṛṣaka, son of Subala.

sanskrit: tato 'rjunaḥ śaravrātair nānāpraharaṇair api gāndhārān vyākulāṃś cakre saubalapramukhān punaḥ
english: Then with floods of arrows and weapons of many kinds Arjuna once more threw into confusion the Gāndhāras led by the son of Subala.

sanskrit: tataḥ pañcaśatān vīrān gāndhārān udyatāyudhān prāhiṇon mṛtyulokāya kruddho bāṇair dhanaṃjayaḥ
english: Then in his wrath Dhanaṃjaya sped five hundred heroic Gāndhāras, their weapons upraised, with his shafts to the realm of Death.

sanskrit: hatāśvāt tu rathāt tūrṇam avatīrya mahābhujaḥ āruroha rathaṃ bhrātur anyac ca dhanur ādade
english: Quickly leaping down from his car whose horses were slain, the mighty-armed one mounted his brother's chariot and took up another bow.

sanskrit: tāv ekaratham ārūḍhau bhrātarau vṛṣakācalau śaravarṣeṇa bībhatsum avidhyetāṃ punaḥ punaḥ
english: The two brothers Vṛṣaka and Acala, mounted now on a single car, pierced Bībhatsu again and again with a rain of arrows.

sanskrit: syālau tava mahātmānau rājānau vṛṣakācalau bhṛśaṃ nijaghnatuḥ pārtham indraṃ vṛtrabalāv iva
english: Your two great-souled brothers-in-law, the kings Vṛṣaka and Acala, smote Pārtha grievously, as the hosts of Vṛtra once smote Indra.

sanskrit: labdhalakṣyau tu gāndhārāv ahatāṃ pāṇḍavaṃ punaḥ nidāghavārṣikau māsau lokaṃ gharmāmbubhir yathā
english: The two Gāndhāras, sure of their aim, struck the Pāṇḍava once more, as the months of summer and the rains drench the world with heat and water.

sanskrit: tau rathasthau naravyāghrau rājānau vṛṣakācalau saṃśliṣṭāṅgau sthitau rājañ jaghānaikeṣuṇārjunaḥ
english: Those tigers among men, the kings Vṛṣaka and Acala, standing upon the car with bodies close pressed together, O king, Arjuna slew with a single arrow.

sanskrit: tau rathāt siṃhasaṃkāśau lohitākṣau mahābhujau gatāsū petatur vīrau sodaryāv ekalakṣaṇau
english: Lion-like, red-eyed, mighty-armed, those two heroes—born of one mother and alike in every mark—fell lifeless from the car.

sanskrit: tayor dehau rathād bhūmiṃ gatau bandhujanapriyau yaśo daśa diśaḥ puṇyaṃ gamayitvā vyavasthitau
english: The bodies of those two, beloved of their kinsmen, went from the car to the earth, having sent their holy fame abroad to the ten directions, where it stood fast.

sanskrit: dṛṣṭvā vinihatau saṃkhye mātulāv apalāyinau bhṛśaṃ mumucur aśrūṇi putrās tava viśāṃ pate
english: Seeing their uncles, who never fled, slain in the fight, your sons, O lord of peoples, shed tears in plenty.

sanskrit: nihatau bhrātarau dṛṣṭvā māyāśataviśāradaḥ kṛṣṇau saṃmohayan māyāṃ vidadhe śakunis tataḥ
english: Seeing his brothers slain, Śakuni, skilled in a hundred sorceries, then wove an illusion to bewilder the two Kṛṣṇas.

sanskrit: laguḍāyoguḍāśmānaḥ śataghnyaś ca saśaktayaḥ gadāparighanistriṃśaśūlamudgarapaṭṭiśāḥ
english: Cudgels, iron balls, stones, and śataghnīs together with javelins; maces, iron bars, swords, spears, hammers, and battle-axes—

sanskrit: sakampanarṣṭinakharā musalāni paraśvadhāḥ kṣurāḥ kṣurapranālīkā vatsadantās trisaṃdhinaḥ
english: lances, double-edged blades, and clawed weapons, pestles and broad-axes, razors and razor-edged tubular darts, calf-tooth shafts and three-jointed missiles,

sanskrit: cakrāṇi viśikhāḥ prāsā vividhāny āyudhāni ca prapetuḥ sarvato digbhyaḥ pradigbhyaś cārjunaṃ prati
english: discs, barbed arrows, and pikes, and weapons of every kind, fell upon Arjuna from all the quarters and the points between.

sanskrit: kharoṣṭramahiṣāḥ siṃhā vyāghrāḥ sṛmaracillikāḥ ṛkṣāḥ sālāvṛkā gṛdhrāḥ kapayo 'tha sarīsṛpāḥ
english: Asses, camels, and buffaloes, lions, tigers, and antelopes and hawks, bears, wolves, and vultures, apes, and creeping serpents,

sanskrit: vividhāni ca rakṣāṃsi kṣudhitāny arjunaṃ prati saṃkruddhāny abhyadhāvanta vividhāni vayāṃsi ca
english: and demons of many kinds, ravenous and enraged, rushed against Arjuna, together with birds of every sort.

sanskrit: tato divyāstravic chūraḥ kuntīputro dhanaṃjayaḥ visṛjann iṣujālāni sahasā tāny atāḍayat
english: Then the valiant son of Kuntī, Dhanaṃjaya, knower of celestial weapons, loosing nets of arrows, struck them all down at once.

sanskrit: te hanyamānāḥ śūreṇa pravaraiḥ sāyakair dṛḍhaiḥ viruvanto mahārāvān vineśuḥ sarvato hatāḥ
english: Smitten by the hero with his choicest, sturdy shafts, they shrieked with mighty cries and perished, slain on every side.

sanskrit: tatas tamaḥ prādurabhūd arjunasya rathaṃ prati tasmāc ca tamaso vācaḥ krūrāḥ pārtham abhartsayan
english: Then a darkness arose before Arjuna's car, and out of that darkness cruel voices reviled Pārtha.

sanskrit: tat tamo 'streṇa mahatā jyotiṣeṇārjuno 'vadhīt hate tasmiñ jalaughās tu prādurāsan bhayānakāḥ
english: That darkness Arjuna slew with the great weapon of light; and when it was destroyed, terrible floods of water appeared.

sanskrit: ambhasas tasya nāśārtham ādityāstram athārjunaḥ prāyuṅktāmbhas tatas tena prāyaśo 'streṇa śoṣitam
english: To destroy that water Arjuna then employed the weapon of the Sun, and by it the flood was for the most part dried away.

sanskrit: evaṃ bahuvidhā māyāḥ saubalasya kṛtāḥ kṛtāḥ jaghānāstrabalenāśu prahasann arjunas tadā
english: Thus the manifold illusions wrought again and again by the son of Subala, Arjuna, laughing, swiftly destroyed by the power of his weapons.

sanskrit: tathā hatāsu māyāsu trasto 'rjunaśarāhataḥ apāyāj javanair aśvaiḥ śakuniḥ prākṛto yathā
english: When his illusions were thus undone, Śakuni, struck by Arjuna's shafts and seized with terror, fled away on his swift horses like a common man.

sanskrit: tato 'rjuno 'stravic chraiṣṭhyaṃ darśayann ātmano 'riṣu abhyavarṣac charaugheṇa kauravāṇām anīkinīm
english: Then Arjuna, displaying among his foes the supremacy of his skill in weapons, rained down a flood of arrows upon the host of the Kauravas.

sanskrit: sā hanyamānā pārthena putrasya tava vāhinī dvaidhībhūtā mahārāja gaṅgevāsādya parvatam
english: That army of your son, smitten by Pārtha, split in two, O great king, like the Gaṅgā when she meets a mountain.

sanskrit: droṇam evānvapadyanta ke cit tatra mahārathāḥ ke cid duryodhanaṃ rājann ardyamānāḥ kirīṭinā
english: Some of the great car-warriors there made their way to Droṇa, and some, O king, sore pressed by the Diademed One, to Duryodhana.

sanskrit: nāpaśyāma tatas tv etat sainyaṃ vai tamasāvṛtam gāṇḍīvasya ca nirghoṣaḥ śruto dakṣiṇato mayā
english: After that we could not see that host, veiled as it was in darkness; but the twang of the Gāṇḍīva I heard upon the right.

sanskrit: śaṅkhadundubhinirghoṣaṃ vāditrāṇāṃ ca nisvanam gāṇḍīvasya ca nirghoṣo vyatikramyāspṛśad divam
english: The blare of conches and kettledrums and the sound of the instruments—the twang of the Gāṇḍīva overtopped them all and touched the heavens.

sanskrit: tataḥ punar dakṣiṇataḥ saṃgrāmaś citrayodhinām suyuddham arjunasyāsīd ahaṃ tu droṇam anvagām
english: Then again on the right was the battle of those who fight in wondrous fashion; well fought was Arjuna's contest, but I followed after Droṇa.

sanskrit: nānāvidhāny anīkāni putrāṇāṃ tava bhārata arjuno vyadhamat kāle divīvābhrāṇi mārutaḥ
english: The hosts of your sons, of many kinds, O Bhārata, Arjuna scattered, as in due season the wind scatters the clouds in the sky.

sanskrit: taṃ vāsavam ivāyāntaṃ bhūrivarṣaśaraughiṇam maheṣvāsaṃ naravyāghraṃ nograṃ kaś cid avārayat
english: As he came on like Vāsava, pouring down great floods of arrows, that mighty bowman, that tiger among men—none could stay him.

sanskrit: te hanyamānāḥ pārthena tvadīyā vyathitā bhṛśam svān eva bahavo jaghnur vidravantas tatas tataḥ
english: Your men, smitten by Pārtha and grievously distressed, many of them in their flight hither and thither slew their own comrades.

sanskrit: te 'rjunena śarā muktāḥ kaṅkapatrās tanucchidaḥ śalabhā iva saṃpetuḥ saṃvṛṇvānā diśo daśa
english: The arrows loosed by Arjuna, heron-feathered and rending the body, fell like locusts, covering the ten directions.

sanskrit: turagaṃ rathinaṃ nāgaṃ padātim api māriṣa vinirbhidya kṣitiṃ jagmur valmīkam iva pannagāḥ
english: Piercing through horse and car-warrior, elephant and foot-soldier alike, O sire, they entered the earth like serpents entering an anthill.

sanskrit: na ca dvitīyaṃ vyasṛjat kuñjarāśvanareṣu saḥ pṛthag ekaśarārugṇā nipetus te gatāsavaḥ
english: Not a second arrow did he loose against elephant, horse, or man; each, struck by a single shaft, fell down bereft of life.

sanskrit: hatair manuṣyais turagaiś ca sarvataḥ; śarābhivṛṣṭair dviradaiś ca pātitaiḥ tadā śvagomāyubaḍābhināditaṃ; vicitram āyodhaśiro babhūva ha
english: With slain men and horses everywhere, and elephants struck down beneath the rain of arrows, the field of battle, loud with the cries of dogs and jackals and crows, became a strange and dreadful sight.

sanskrit: pitā sutaṃ tyajati suhṛdvaraṃ suhṛt; tathaiva putraḥ pitaraṃ śarāturaḥ svarakṣaṇe kṛtamatayas tadā janās; tyajanti vāhān api pārthapīḍitāḥ
english: The father forsook the son, the friend his dearest friend, and the son likewise forsook his father, tormented by the arrows; bent now only upon saving themselves, men harried by Pārtha abandoned even their mounts.

sanskrit: dhṛtarāṣṭra uvāca teṣv anīkeṣu bhagneṣu pāṇḍuputreṇa saṃjaya calitānāṃ drutānāṃ ca katham āsīn mano hi vaḥ
english: Dhṛtarāṣṭra said: When those hosts were broken by the son of Pāṇḍu, O Saṃjaya, what was the temper of your minds as you wavered and took to flight?

sanskrit: anīkānāṃ prabhagnānāṃ vyavasthānam apaśyatām duṣkaraṃ pratisaṃdhānaṃ tan mamācakṣva saṃjaya
english: Hard is it to rally hosts once shattered, when men can see no place to make their stand; tell me of that, Saṃjaya.

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca tathāpi tava putrasya priyakāmā viśāṃ pate yaśaḥ pravīrā lokeṣu rakṣanto droṇam anvayuḥ
english: Saṃjaya said: Even so, O lord of peoples, seeking your son's good, those heroes, guarding their fame throughout the worlds, followed after Droṇa.

sanskrit: samudyateṣu śastreṣu saṃprāpte ca yudhiṣṭhire akurvann āryakarmāṇi bhairave satyabhītavat
english: With weapons upraised, and Yudhiṣṭhira drawing near, in that fearful hour they wrought the deeds of noble men, like those who fear to break their word.

sanskrit: antaraṃ bhīmasenasya prāpatann amitaujasaḥ sātyakeś caiva śūrasya dhṛṣṭadyumnasya cābhibho
english: They sought to find an opening upon Bhīmasena of measureless might, and upon the valiant Sātyaki, and upon Dhṛṣṭadyumna, O lord.

sanskrit: droṇaṃ droṇam iti krūrāḥ pāñcālāḥ samacodayan mā droṇam iti putrās te kurūn sarvān acodayan
english: "Droṇa! Droṇa!" the fierce Pāñcālas urged one another on; "Not Droṇa!" your sons cried, rousing all the Kurus.

sanskrit: droṇaṃ droṇam iti hy eke mā droṇam iti cāpare kurūṇāṃ pāṇḍavānāṃ ca droṇadyūtam avartata
english: "Droṇa! Droṇa!" cried the one side, "Not Droṇa!" the other; between the Kurus and the Pāṇḍavas a gambling-match for Droṇa was being played.

sanskrit: yaṃ yaṃ sma bhajate droṇaḥ pāñcālānāṃ rathavrajam tatra tatra sma pāñcālyo dhṛṣṭadyumno 'tha dhīyate
english: Whatever band of Pāñcāla cars Droṇa fell upon, there at once the Pāñcāla prince Dhṛṣṭadyumna was set against him.

sanskrit: yathābhāgaviparyāse saṃgrāme bhairave sati vīrāḥ samāsadan vīrān agacchan bhīravaḥ parān
english: As the appointed ranks were thrown into confusion in that terrible battle, hero closed with hero, and the cowards went against the foe.

sanskrit: akampanīyāḥ śatrūṇāṃ babhūvus tatra pāṇḍavāḥ akampayaṃs tv anīkāni smarantaḥ kleśam ātmanaḥ
english: There the Pāṇḍavas stood unshaken by their enemies, and they shook the hostile hosts, remembering their own afflictions.

sanskrit: te tv amarṣavaśaṃ prāptā hrīmantaḥ sattvacoditāḥ tyaktvā prāṇān nyavartanta ghnanto droṇaṃ mahāhave
english: Yielding to wrath, full of self-respect and driven by their courage, they turned back ready to give up their lives, striving to slay Droṇa in that great battle.

sanskrit: ayasām iva saṃpātaḥ śilānām iva cābhavat dīvyatāṃ tumule yuddhe prāṇair amitatejasām
english: It was like the clash of iron, like the crash of stones, as those men of boundless splendour gambled with their very lives in the tumultuous fight.

sanskrit: na tu smaranti saṃgrāmam api vṛddhās tathāvidham dṛṣṭapūrvaṃ mahārāja śrutapūrvam athāpi vā
english: Not even the aged could recall a battle of such a kind, O great king, ever before seen or ever before heard.

sanskrit: prākampateva pṛthivī tasmin vīrāvasādane pravartatā balaughena mahatā bhārapīḍitā
english: The earth seemed to tremble in that destruction of heroes, weighed down and oppressed by the great flood of armies surging upon her.

sanskrit: ghūrṇato hi balaughasya divaṃ stabdhveva nisvanaḥ ajātaśatroḥ kruddhasya putrasya tava cābhavat
english: From the reeling flood of warriors a roar arose, of the wrathful Ajātaśatru and of your son, as though it filled and stilled the very sky.

sanskrit: samāsādya tu pāṇḍūnām anīkāni sahasraśaḥ droṇena caratā saṃkhye prabhagnāni śitaiḥ śaraiḥ
english: As Droṇa ranged through the battle, the hosts of the Pāṇḍavas, met by him in their thousands, were broken by his keen arrows.

sanskrit: teṣu pramathyamāneṣu droṇenādbhutakarmaṇā paryavārayad āsādya droṇaṃ senāpatiḥ svayam
english: As they were being crushed by Droṇa of wondrous deeds, the commander himself drew near and beset Droṇa on every side.

sanskrit: tad adbhutam abhūd yuddhaṃ droṇapāñcālyayos tadā naiva tasyopamā kā cit saṃbhaved iti me matiḥ
english: Wondrous then was the combat of Droṇa and the Pāñcāla prince; to it, I think, no comparison could be found.

sanskrit: tato nīlo 'nalaprakhyo dadāha kuruvāhinīm śarasphuliṅgaś cāpārcir dahan kakṣam ivānalaḥ
english: Then Nīla, bright as fire, burned the Kuru army, his arrows for sparks and his bow for flame, like a fire consuming dry grass.

sanskrit: taṃ dahantam anīkāni droṇaputraḥ pratāpavān pūrvābhibhāṣī suślakṣṇaṃ smayamāno 'bhyabhāṣata
english: As he burned the hosts, the valorous son of Droṇa, speaking first and very smoothly, smiling, addressed him:

sanskrit: nīla kiṃ bahubhir dagdhais tava yodhaiḥ śarārciṣā mayaikena hi yudhyasva kruddhaḥ prahara cāśugaiḥ
english: "Nīla, what use are the many warriors you have burned with your flaming shafts? Fight with me alone; in your wrath, strike at me with your swift arrows."

sanskrit: taṃ padmanikarākāraṃ padmapatranibhekṣaṇam vyākośapadmābhamukhaṃ nīlo vivyādha sāyakaiḥ
english: Him, who had the hue of a cluster of lotuses, whose eyes were like lotus-petals, whose face shone like a full-blown lotus, Nīla pierced with his shafts.

sanskrit: tenātividdhaḥ sahasā drauṇir bhallaiḥ śitais tribhiḥ dhanur dhvajaṃ ca chatraṃ ca dviṣataḥ sa nyakṛntata
english: Sorely pierced by him, the son of Droṇa straightway, with three sharp broad-headed shafts, cut down his enemy's bow and banner and parasol.

sanskrit: sotplutya syandanāt tasmān nīlaś carmavarāsidhṛk droṇāyaneḥ śiraḥ kāyād dhartum aicchat patatrivat
english: Leaping down from his car, Nīla, bearing fine shield and sword, sought to take the head from the body of the son of Droṇa, swift as a bird.

sanskrit: tasyodyatāseḥ sunasaṃ śiraḥ kāyāt sakuṇḍalam bhallenāpāharad drauṇiḥ smayamāna ivānagha
english: As his sword was upraised, the son of Droṇa, smiling as it were, O sinless one, struck off with a broad-headed shaft that fair-nosed head with its earrings from the body.

sanskrit: saṃpūrṇacandrābhamukhaḥ padmapatranibhekṣaṇaḥ prāṃśur utpalagarbhābho nihato nyapatat kṣitau
english: His face bright as the full moon, his eyes like lotus-petals, tall and of the hue of a lotus's inner bloom, he fell slain to the earth.

sanskrit: tataḥ pravivyathe senā pāṇḍavī bhṛśam ākulā ācāryaputreṇa hate nīle jvalitatejasi
english: Then the Pāṇḍava army was sorely shaken and thrown into confusion, when Nīla of blazing splendour was slain by the teacher's son.

sanskrit: acintayaṃś ca te sarve pāṇḍavānāṃ mahārathāḥ kathaṃ no vāsavis trāyāc chatrubhya iti māriṣa
english: And all the great car-warriors of the Pāṇḍavas thought to themselves, O sire: "How shall the son of Vāsava deliver us from our foes?"

sanskrit: dakṣiṇena tu senāyāḥ kurute kadanaṃ balī saṃśaptakāvaśeṣasya nārāyaṇabalasya ca
english: Meanwhile, on the right of the army, the mighty one was making havoc of what remained of the Saṃśaptakas and of the Nārāyaṇa host.

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca pratighātaṃ tu sainyasya nāmṛṣyata vṛkodaraḥ so 'bhinad bāhlikaṃ ṣaṣṭyā karṇaṃ ca daśabhiḥ śaraiḥ
english: Saṃjaya said: But Vṛkodara could not endure this check to the host; he pierced Bāhlika with sixty shafts and Karṇa with ten.

sanskrit: tasya droṇaḥ śitair bāṇais tīkṣṇadhārair ayasmayaiḥ jīvitāntam abhiprepsur marmaṇy āśu jaghāna ha
english: At him Droṇa, with keen iron arrows of sharp edge, seeking to end his life, swiftly struck at his vital parts.

sanskrit: karṇo dvādaśabhir bāṇair aśvatthāmā ca saptabhiḥ ṣaḍbhir duryodhano rājā tata enam avākirat
english: Karṇa with twelve arrows, Aśvatthāman with seven, and King Duryodhana with six then covered him over.

sanskrit: bhīmaseno 'pi tān sarvān pratyavidhyan mahābalaḥ droṇaṃ pañcāśateṣūṇāṃ karṇaṃ ca daśabhiḥ śaraiḥ
english: Bhīmasena too, of great might, pierced them all in return: Droṇa with fifty arrows, Karṇa with ten,

sanskrit: duryodhanaṃ dvādaśabhir drauṇiṃ cāṣṭābhir āśugaiḥ ārāvaṃ tumulaṃ kurvann abhyavartata tān raṇe
english: Duryodhana with twelve, and the son of Droṇa with eight swift shafts; raising a tumultuous roar, he bore down upon them in the fight.

sanskrit: tasmin saṃtyajati prāṇān mṛtyusādhāraṇīkṛte ajātaśatrus tān yodhān bhīmaṃ trātety acodayat
english: As he, ready to give up his life, was bringing it level with death itself, Ajātaśatru urged on his warriors, crying, "Save Bhīma!"
